messages:
sanjay: Hey team — planning to work from Toronto for ~4 months (May->Aug). Quick Qs: will my WFH stipend be prorated? Do I need to switch payroll or benefits? Any tax nexus concerns I should flag?
elaine: Congrats on the trip! :party_parrot: Short answers: stipend = prorated, benefits continue for short moves but payroll/tax depends on duration. Need to gather dates and manager sign-off.
mike: cc @elaine — I've approved the dates on my side. Sanjay, can you put the exact start/end in the form?
sanjay: Thanks — start 2027-05-10, back 2027-09-01. Submitted the temporary-location form just now. Link: https://hr.redwood.example/temporary-location
people-ops-bot: Thanks for submitting the Temporary Location Change form, sanjay. A People Ops rep will review within 3 business days. Required: manager approval, travel proof (if requested), and final payroll decision.
elaine: Okay saw the form. A few practical notes: 1) WFH stipend — we prorate monthly days while you're away. 2) If your absence is under 90 days total in a 12-mo window, we usually keep you on US payroll. 3) Between 90–183 days, we run a tax/nexus review (legal + payroll). 4) Over 183 days typically requires local payroll and benefits/localization.
sanjay: Good to know. How does the prorate calc work?
elaine: We do a calendar-day prorate. Example we shared earlier: 
```
monthly_stipend = $200
may_days = 22 (workdays in May while remote)
may_prorated = (22 / total_workdays_in_may) * monthly_stipend
```
We handle it automatically once Payroll gets the approved form.
payroll-bot: Payroll queue updated: ticket #PR-2987 created for sanjay. Payroll will confirm pay treatment and any withholding changes within 5 business days.
sanjay: Will health insurance/401k vesting be affected?
elaine: Short term moves don't change 401k vesting schedule or active benefits. If we need to move you to local payroll (>183d) we'll coordinate benefits transition and explain contributions.
mike: One more — any travel visa requirement we should check?
elaine: For Canada, many US citizens can work remotely short-term without a work permit, but tax/residency is separate. We recommend you keep travel records (dates in/out). People Ops/legal will reach out if deeper review is needed.
sanjay: Great — appreciate the clarity. Anything I should track while I'm there?
elaine: Please: 1) keep travel logs, 2) update Homebase profile with temporary address, 3) upload your manager approval to the form thread, and 4) ping payroll thread if you get any local tax letters.
sanjay: Will do. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
people-ops-bot: Thread closed for new submissions — People Ops will follow up on PR-2987. If anything changes, reopen the form or DM @elaine.
